heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 Mini easily runs Overture Rock PLA at speeds up to 190 mm/s capped by a 16 mm³/s maximum volumetric flow rate. However, you must upgrade the stock stainless steel hotend to a Bambu hardened steel nozzle assembly to prevent rapid bore wear from the abrasive rock speckle particulates.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate cleaned with dish soap and warm water (no adhesive required)
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 16 mm³/s in the filament settings to maintain consistent matte finish and avoid under-extrusion at high speeds.
Lower Outer Wall Speed to 100-120 mm/s to ensure consistent surface texture and hide layer lines uniformly with the matte stone particles.
Increase Default Printing Temperature to 210°C-215°C when using a hardened steel nozzle to compensate for its lower thermal conductivity compared to brass or stainless steel.
Set Pressure Advance to 0.024-0.028 s via OrcaSlicer dynamic calibration to eliminate corner bulging caused by particulate drag in the melt zone.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Premature Nozzle Wear and Inconsistent Extrusion
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: The rock composite micro-particles rapidly erode the stock 0.4mm stainless steel nozzle orifice, altering diameter and backpressure.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Install the official Bambu Lab 0.4mm Hardened Steel Hotend assembly and select Hardened Steel Nozzle in the printer device settings.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Intermittent Clogging or Heat Creep in Extruder
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Aggressive retract-on-layer-change cycles pull particulate-laden semi-molten PLA past the heat break inside the compact direct-drive extruder.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Limit retraction distance to 0.8 mm max, disable 'Retract on layer change', and verify the extruder cold block cooling fan is operating at 100%.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Weak Layer Adhesion or Chalky Brittle Breaks
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Printing near the bottom of the recommended temperature range (below 205°C) with full part cooling reduces polymer chain entanglement around the mineral fillers.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Raise printing temperature to 215°C and reduce Part Cooling Fan to 70% min / 85% max in OrcaSlicer filament cooling settings.

faq.question: Can I print Overture Rock PLA with the stock stainless steel nozzle that came with the A1 Mini?
faq.answer: Technically it will feed, but it will quickly enlarge the nozzle bore and ruin dimensional accuracy within 200-500 grams of printing. A Bambu hardened steel hotend upgrade is strongly recommended.

faq.question: Does Overture Rock PLA work reliably in the Bambu AMS Lite?
faq.answer: Yes, standard 1kg plastic spools of Overture Rock PLA fit and feed reliably on the AMS Lite rotary spindles, though cardboard spool versions require an adapter ring to avoid slipping.

faq.question: Why does the surface look glossy in some areas and matte in others?
faq.answer: Variable printing speeds cause melt temperature variations; slower sections look glossier while faster sections appear matte. Enforcing an outer wall speed limit of 100-120 mm/s locks in a uniform matte finish.

faq.question: Does Overture Rock PLA require drying before printing?
faq.answer: Standard PLA is not strongly hygroscopic and usually prints well out of the sealed pouch, but drying at 45°C-50°C for 4 hours will eliminate micro-stringing caused by moisture absorbed by the mineral additives.
